citation.title: Real-time measurement of ion temperature and relative hydrogenic plasma composition by active charge exchange

topic: Proposed active charge-exchange neutral-particle-analyser method to infer local main-ion (hydrogenic) Ti and isotope ratio from fluxes at two equal-velocity energy pairs.
own_question: Can Ti and relative H/D/T composition be obtained in real time from doping-beam CX fluxes without other plasma or beam parameters?
actual_method_and_evidence: Analytic derivation assuming Maxwellian species at equal temperature. It also includes error propagation, qualitative discussion of scattering and halo effects, and a helium-beam argument referencing prior reports. No experimental demonstration, implementation or measured latency is reported. The roughly 100 ms pulse length is an estimate.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Real-time ion-temperature and fuel-mix information has long been framed as a control need; one early proposal derived Ti from active CX neutral fluxes via a closed-form ratio.
claim_checks.qualification: This was a theoretical proposal for main-ion NPA, not CES impurity spectroscopy, and was not demonstrated. Equations extracted poorly.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs were neutral fluxes integrated over a beam pulse of an estimated 100-200 ms. This is a direct measurement, not nowcasting, and the timing is not measured.
forbidden_inferences: That the method was implemented or validated
That it concerns carbon-impurity CES Ti
That its timescale is comparable to our 10 ms grid
That it shows prior Ti diagnostics are all non-real-time beyond the author's 1992 view
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional historical citation for the motivation behind real-time Ti. The diagnostic, species and approach differ from ours, and the source provides no evidence.
